title: BK polyomavirus nephropathy

steps.tx: **BK polyomavirus** is a double-stranded circular DNA virus that resides latently in recipient and donor renal tubular epithelial and urothelial cells, reactivating under potent immunosuppression (particularly tacrolimus and MMF regimens). This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice, reflecting reactivation.

steps.tx: **Decoy cells** are urothelial cells with characteristic ground-glass, enlarged basophilic intranuclear viral inclusion bodies, detectable in urine cytology during early BK viruria. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice. Comprehensive nephrology clinical assessment confirms these core diagnostic findings.

steps.tx: **KDIGO** guidelines recommend routine screening for BK virus replication with plasma quantitative PCR monthly for the first 3 to 6 months post-transplant, then every 3 months until 12 months, and whenever serum creatinine unexplainedly rises. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.

steps.tx: **Presumptive BK** polyomavirus nephropathy is diagnosed when plasma BK viral load remains persistently >= 10^4 copies/mL (or >= 4.0 log10 copies/mL) for at least 3 weeks. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice, reflecting PCR threshold.

steps.tx: Definitive diagnosis of BK polyomavirus nephropathy (**BKPyVN**) requires allograft biopsy demonstrating intranuclear viral inclusions, tubulitis, interstitial inflammation, and positive immunohistochemical nuclear staining for SV40 large T antigen. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.

steps.tx: **reduction of immunosuppression** is essential. Primary cornerstone of therapy for BKPyVN is stepwise reduction of maintenance immunosuppression (reducing MMF by 50% or stopping it completely, followed by lowering calcineurin inhibitor trough targets by 25% to 50%). This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.

steps.tx: Adjunctive second-line therapies evaluated for refractory BK viremia include **leflunomide** (an active metabolite inhibitor of pyrimidine synthesis with antiviral properties), intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), and cidofovir. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.

steps.tx: Late complications of BK virus replication in the urinary tract include **ureteric stenosis**, ulceration, and obstruction secondary to dense viral-induced inflammation and scarring, as well as hemorrhagic cystitis. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.
